source_review.notes: Reviewed the original Grossi-Gupta-Vitter wavelet-tree paper, Navarro's author-maintained survey and book resources, Claude-Navarro sequence-query paper, Claude-Navarro-Ordonez wavelet-matrix paper, Gagie-Navarro-Puglisi applications paper, and maintained SDSL-lite repository. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Complexity, entropy, and implementation claims remain scoped to their stated shape, support, model, or named library.

evidence: Checked sequence S[0..n), ordered alphabet Sigma, sigma, node subsequences, matrix levels, zero counts, and stable routing notation.
Checked half-open sequence rank and zero-based select match the prerequisite bit-vector convention.
Checked range endpoints, zero-based quantile order, code width, unused codes, and generation metadata remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Tree-node coordinates and wavelet-matrix global-level coordinates are explicitly separated.

evidence: Recomputed BANANA$ sorted alphabet [$,A,B,N] and codes 00/01/10/11.
Recomputed level bitmaps 1010100 and 1110011, zero counts 4 and 2, and stable final order $BAAANN.
Recomputed histogram {$:1,A:3,B:1,N:2} and select positions $:[6], A:[1,3,5], B:[0], N:[2,4].
Recomputed subrange [1,6) as ANANA, sorted AAANN, whose zero-based order 3 is N.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All bounded-fixture values were reproduced independently from the chapter implementation.

evidence: Proved stable partition maps a parent prefix endpoint i to child endpoint rank_b(B,i).
Derived access and known-symbol rank by induction on the path depth.
Derived reverse select using bit-select inversion and subtraction of matrix zero offsets for one branches.
Derived range quantile from zero counts between mapped half-open endpoints and order subtraction on right descent.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The nH0 and lower-order compression discussion is identified as a family/model result rather than a bound for the Python fixture or every implementation.

evidence: Reviewed empty/singleton ranges, all-equal sequences, absent symbols, invalid select ordinals, minimum/maximum quantiles, and zero-length alphabets.
Reviewed non-power-of-two alphabets, unused codes, Unicode normalization, numeric versus lexical order, Huffman codebooks, and malformed symbols.
Reviewed unstable serial/parallel partitions, wrong zero offsets, mixed tree/matrix formulas, padding, overflow, corrupt supports, and truncated mapped sections.
Reviewed static mutation, dynamic support propagation, immutable segments, crash publication, cross-version readers, cache/NUMA behavior, and adversarial skew.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable fixture excludes succinct supports, compression, non-power-of-two code width, Huffman/multiary shapes, updates, mapping, parallel builds, corruption, and large-scale performance.

evidence: Every one of seven symbols contributes one bit to each of two levels and each stable partition preserves branch-relative order.
Access reconstructs every original position and rank totals reproduce the source histogram.
Select positions reproduce every source occurrence and both before/through rank inverse properties hold.
Range quantile matches the independently sorted subrange and exact seventeen-line stdout passes.
invariant_checking.notes: The model validates fixed-width wavelet-matrix routing semantics, not production rank/select complexity or compressed space.

evidence: Reviewed coordinate induction from root sequence to leaf occurrence ordinals.
Reviewed select inversion from final symbol interval through matrix levels to the original position.
Reviewed range-frequency as a difference of prefix ranks and range-quantile branch correctness.
Reviewed fixed-width balanced payload nh and the metadata/support qualifications around total space.
proof_review.notes: No concrete compressed-bitvector theorem, dynamic concurrency proof, external-memory construction proof, or persisted-format recovery proof is claimed.

evidence: Balanced, Huffman, multiary, nodewise, levelwise, and matrix layouts are presented with distinct trade-offs.
Entropy-shaped compression claims are separated from plain routing-bit and finite metadata accounting.
The model explicitly labels scanning rank/select helpers as semantic evidence rather than constant-time succinct operations.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Operational guidance and benchmarking obligations are not presented as consequences of the asymptotic theory.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact seventeen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the safe verifier.
Independent reconstruction reproduced both routing levels, final order, histogram, select lists, quantile input, sorted oracle, and output.
All seven final reference destinations returned HTTP 200 and local structure, links, examples, exercises, answers, and snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No SDSL build, succinct/compressed bitmap implementation, exhaustive all-sequence campaign, dynamic update workload, parallel/external build, mapped-file corruption test, cache benchmark, or production deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives wavelet navigation from stable partition plus rank/select, distinguishes tree and matrix layouts, and carries the model through range queries, shape, space, construction, persistence, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed alphabet order/versioning, parallel stable construction, layout selection, compressed/dynamic variants, metadata accounting, mapped serialization, checksums, atomic publication, corruption validation, query distributions, cache behavior, and build peak.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet states the complete routing model; BANANA$ provides an inspectable matrix; ten examples cover stability, access, rank, select, quantile, frequency, unused codes, shape, parallelism, and corruption; five exercises span construction, proof, tracing, design, and persistence.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/author/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Grossi, Gupta, Vitter, Navarro, Claude, Ordonez, Gagie, Puglisi, SDSL, database, information-retrieval, performance, systems, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production succinct/compressed wavelet tree or matrix, universal entropy bound for a concrete implementation, dynamic concurrency, external-memory construction, mapped persistence/recovery, certification, nor deployment fitness.
